answer: Sybil resistance can ride on randomized physical-presence pings: each agent binds one GPS-fenced site — a mesa ranch, a grove orchard, or a basalt quarry — and must answer a surprise sensor challenge within 2 seconds, returning a signed reading only a device actually there can produce. A farm can't parallelize it: every extra fake needs its own distinct fenced site costing roughly $40 a month plus a human to install the sensor, and the 2-second window stops one rig covering two locations. Duplicate coordinates are rejected on-chain, so one operator cannot cheaply mint a thousand names.
